pamphlet_excerpts: Support Tooth Supportive: Support for the Tooth The supportive tissues of the tooth are called theperiodontium, which includes the periodontalligament, the alveolar bone.
Cementum Periodontal: The cementum, periodontal ligament, andalveolar bone connect the teeth to the jaws.
Whenone Damaged Missing: Whenone of these is damaged or missing, the tooth willloosen and eventually fall out.
Supportivetissues Actually: The supportivetissues actually get stronger from vigorous use.
step_by_step_procedure: Strong Fiberlike Tissue: This strong, fiberlike tissue anchors theroot to the bone and cushions the surrounding bone againstthe shock of chewing and biting.
Thedentist Cuts Periodontal: When extracting a tooth, thedentist cuts the periodontal ligament that connects the tooth tothe bone.
Bony Part Upper: The bony part of the upper and lower jawsthat surrounds and supports the roots of the teeth and the gumsis called the alveolar bone.
Alveolar Means Hollow: Alveolar means “hollow.” The alveolar bone has hollow places, or sockets, that house the roots ofthe teeth.

(c) Explain the first-aid procedure for saving a tooth that has been knocked out. (d) Discuss how the use of tobacco products can negatively affect your oral health.

pamphlet_excerpts: They Generally Work: They generally work forgovernment agencies such as the United States Public Health Service, the military, hospitals, and universities.
Dentists Thisspecialty Study: Dentists in thisspecialty study trends in dental disease and related disordersand report this information to other dentists.
Specialist Dental Public: A specialist in dental public health must earn anadvanced degree and complete a dental public health residency.
Endodontist Cares Inner: An endodontist cares for the inner parts of the teeth.
step_by_step_procedure: Thisspecialist Concerned: Thisspecialist is concerned with the prevention, diagnosis, andtreatment of disorders of the dental pulp and tissues surroundingthe root.
Endodontist Expert Pulp: The endodontist is an expert in pulp capping, root canal therapy, surgical procedures such as root amputation, and bleaching (for teeth.
Oral Maxillofacial: The oral and maxillofacial pathologist studies tissues from themouth and maxillofacial region and helps diagnose diseasessuch as infections, benign.
She Aresource Person: He or she is aresource person, or consultant, for general dentists and otherspecialists.

pamphlet_excerpts: Out Whether the Water: Find out whether the water inyour home isfluoridated.
Drink Eightglasses Tapwater: If it is, try to drink eightglasses of tapwater each dayand know thatwhile you arereplenishing fluidsin your body, youare also protecting your.
Fluoride Chemical Compound: Fluoride is a chemical compound that forms when fluorinecombines with other elements.
Fluoride reinforces Enamel: After teeth are formed, fluoridereinforces enamel and also acts with minerals in saliva torestore enamel in the earliest stages of decay.
step_by_step_procedure: Fluoride Present Everywhere: Fluoride is present everywhere, in varying amounts.
Concentration Fluorides Soil: The concentration of fluorides in the soil, water, and plantsin certain areas may be lower or higher than in other areas.
Fluoride Internally Applyit: You can take fluoride internally or applyit directly to the surfaces of the teeth.
Fluoridation Adding Fluoride: Fluoridation, or adding fluoride to our water supply, is oneway health officials help protect public health.

pamphlet_excerpts: Healthy Peopleproduce Cups: Healthy peopleproduce about 6 cups of saliva a day.
Eat Affect Dental: When and how often you eat may affect your dental healthmore than what and how much you eat.
Don Giveup Sugar: You don’t have to giveup sugar to protect your teeth.
Eat Sweet Foods: If you eat sweet foods anddrinks only at mealtimes and faithfully brush and floss your teeth afterward, you can usually avoid tooth decay.
step_by_step_procedure: Extra Saliva Produced: The extra saliva produced to digest a meal will help washaway or neutralize acids, but eating sugary foods between meals will keep the acid level.
Choose Foods Low: If you mustsnack, choose foods that are low in sugar content: peanuts, popcorn, pretzels, olives, eggs, meats, milk, and plain yogurt.
Snacking Bedtime Harmful: Snacking before bedtime is harmful because of the reduced production of saliva during sleep.
Plaque Remains Undisturbedon: The plaque remains undisturbedon the teeth for hours.

requirements.req_text: Do TWO of the following: (a) Make a model tooth out of soap, clay, paper-mâché, or wax. Using a string and a large hand brush, show your troop or a school class proper tooth-brushing and flossing procedures. (b) Make a poster on the prevention of dental disease. Show the importance of good oral health. (c) Collect at least five advertisements for different toothpastes. List the claims that each one makes. Tell about the accuracy of the advertisements. (d) Write a feature story for your school newspaper on the proper care of teeth and gums. Include in your story how the use of tobacco products can negatively affect a person's oral health. (e) Make drawings and write about the progress of dental decay. Describe the types of dental filling and treatments a dentist can use to repair dental decay problems.
